title: Which part of the bird does each model select?
caption: Four multimodal-model rows compare the original image, predicted box mask, SAM-refined mask, and overlay. These are individual examples; the paper reports aggregate performance separately.
alt: Four model rows compare boxes and object masks for a bird in flight.
credit: Original figure from Caliskan and Chen, LUMOS.

title: The same lamp, different localizations
caption: A lamp example shows how different model localizations feed into the mask-refinement stage. A segmentation model can refine a useful box but cannot reliably repair a box placed over the wrong region.
alt: Four model rows compare masks and overlays for a red lamp on a table.
credit: Original figure from Caliskan and Chen, LUMOS.

title: Unusual observations as research leads
caption: Candidate outliers identified by the top methods are projected with CBLOF and robust scaling. Examples include post-conflict GDP changes and unusual combinations of health spending and health outcomes. The flagged cases invite substantive checking.
alt: Three panels show candidate country-year outliers with accompanying country labels.
credit: Original figure from Caliskan, Lelko, Noe, and Ogawa, ACROSS.

title: How many known outliers were recovered?
caption: The ensemble recovers about 54% of the labelled outlier observations on average, compared with about 15% for the Cook’s distance baseline. The benchmark contains 14 tasks with incomplete outlier labels; recall and F1 should be read in that context.
alt: Original comparison table with mean recall near 0.54 for ACROSS and 0.15 for Cook’s distance.
credit: Original table from Caliskan, Lelko, Noe, and Ogawa, ACROSS.

title: What the vegetation detector keeps
caption: Five panorama pairs show the original street-level image on the left and DEVISE output on the right, with detected vegetation emphasized in green. The examples illustrate measurement behavior rather than a quantitative accuracy benchmark.
alt: Five paired street panoramas compare the original view with highlighted detected vegetation.
credit: Original figure from the DEVISE manuscript. Street imagery © Google.

title: Three counties, two ways to count greenery
caption: The top row maps the sampled Street View locations in Bucks, Dauphin, and Washington counties. The next rows compare plain pixel-count greenness with depth-aware estimates; colors are normalized across the panorama corpus.
alt: Nine maps show sampled locations, baseline greenery, and depth-aware greenery for three U.S. counties.
credit: Original figure from the DEVISE manuscript.

title: Mapping generated profiles beside survey responses
caption: Rows use mean, median, and modal response summaries; columns use PCA, UMAP, and t-SNE. Larger squares represent generated scholar profiles and smaller circles represent contemporary country aggregates. The projections are exploratory, not validation of a historical thinker’s beliefs.
alt: Nine scatterplots compare generated scholar profiles and contemporary country aggregates under three projection methods.
credit: Original figure from Caliskan and colleagues, HalalLLM vs. KosherLLM.

title: The response pattern behind an average
caption: Median responses are displayed by survey item and scholar–model combination. Color shows the coded response value; white marks responses outside the acceptable range. Different items use different scales, so color alone is not a common ideological score.
alt: Dense heatmap of median coded World Values Survey responses across scholar and model combinations.
credit: Original figure from Caliskan and colleagues, HalalLLM vs. KosherLLM.
